status_observed: 500 {"detail":"Internal server error"} â€” four independent invalid-value cases
what_is_wrong: upsert_server_settings has no try/except around db.commit() at all, so every DB-level rejection surfaces as an unhandled 500 rather than a validation error. Four reachable cases: an encryption value outside STARTTLS/SSL_TLS/NONE (ck_ess_encryption), a provider outside the five allowed (ck_ess_provider), switching provider to a non-CUSTOM_SMTP value without supplying api_key (ck_ess_api_key), and smtp_port outside 1..65535 (ck_ess_port). None of these are validated in EmailServerSettingsWrite, so the API accepts the body and then blows up. The provider-switch case is the realistic one: an admin moving from Custom SMTP to Mailgun and saving before pasting the key gets a 500.
suspected_cause: D:\Projects\Company Management Software\backend\app\api\v1\masters_email_config.py:137 (bare `await db.commit()` in upsert_server_settings, no DBAPIError catch and no Pydantic enum validation on provider/encryption)

what_is_wrong: set-default accepts a deactivated account and makes it the company default, producing exactly the is_default=true + is_active=false state that the deactivate endpoint and the DB trigger trg_bank_accounts_reject_deactivate_default exist to prevent. The trigger only fires when OLD.is_default=1 AND NEW.is_default=1 AND NEW.is_active=0, so approaching the same state from the other direction (row already inactive, then flipped to default) passes unchecked. The resulting default account does not even appear in GET /masters/bank-accounts/options, which is active-only, so downstream pickers cannot show or resolve the company's own default.
